**Subject: RE: Program coordination – summer wrap-up and community feedback**

**From:** Priya Singh
**To:** Maya Chen; Tom Okafor
**Cc:**
**Date:** Tuesday, 24 November 2026, 3:42 PM

Hi Maya, Tom,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the roster notes – I’ve added everything to the shared calendar and I’ll chase Marcus and Aisha again tomorrow morning. Before we lock in the December schedule, I wanted to share some community feedback that came through over the last week. A few of these came in via the suggestion box, a couple were sent directly to the front desk, and one came through the library’s Facebook page. I’ve grouped them roughly by program area so we can decide what’s worth acting on before the summer rush.

**Feedback on recent programs**

1. **Seniors’ morning tea (Tuesday 10 November)** – One attendee, Margaret, left a note saying she really enjoyed the session but found the room a bit cold. She suggested we check the air-conditioning before next time. I’ve put a maintenance request in, but it might be worth adding “check room temp” to the run sheet for December. Nothing urgent, just a comfort thing.

2. **Baby Bounce (Thursday sessions)** – A parent, Sarah, emailed the front desk to say the 10:00 session has been filling up quickly and she’s been turned away twice. She asked if we could add a second session or increase the capacity. I know we’ve had this conversation before – the room can hold about 20 families comfortably, and we’re usually at that limit by 9:45. I’m not sure we can add another session without extra staff, but I thought it was worth raising again given the school holidays are coming.

3. **Lego Club (Saturday sessions)** – Tom, you mentioned you had a parent ask about age ranges after the last session. Just to confirm, the flyer says ages 5–12, but we’ve been letting younger siblings join in if they’re supervised. One parent suggested we put a sign up clarifying that, so we don’t get any awkward conversations at the door. Happy to draft something if you think it’s useful.

4. **Author talk (Wednesday 18 November)** – This one came through the Facebook page. A regular attendee, David, said he enjoyed the talk but would love to see more local authors in the program. He specifically mentioned a couple of names – I’ve pasted his comment below so you can see who he meant. I haven’t contacted anyone yet, but if we’re planning the autumn program soon, it might be worth reaching out.

> “Great session tonight. Would love to see more local writers – has the library thought about inviting [name] or [name]? Both have new books out and I think they’d draw a crowd.”

5. **Summer Reading Launch (Monday 28 December)** – We’ve had a few families RSVP already, which is great. One parent asked if there would be face painting again this year – I think we did that in 2024 but not last summer. I’ve noted it as a “maybe” on the planning doc. If we can get a volunteer or a local business to sponsor it, I’m happy to coordinate.

**Suggestions for future programs**

Alongside the feedback, there were a few broader ideas that came through – some more feasible than others. I’ve listed them below so you can see what’s been suggested and we can decide what to take forward.

- **A “Library 101” session for new migrants** – This came from a community worker who attends the English conversation group. She said a few of her clients have mentioned they’re not sure how to use the library catalogue or borrow e-books. We could run a simple workshop in January or February. I think this is a great idea, but I’d want to check with the outreach team to see if they’ve done something similar before.

documents.content:
The venue booking came back from the Events Centre today, reference ECH-2026-1105. I’ve attached the confirmation PDF. They’ve allocated us the Riverside Room, which is the one we wanted, and the setup time is from 9:00 am. The room holds 80 chairs in theatre style, or 60 with the round tables. For the launch we’d planned on the theatre layout plus a couple of tall tables near the door for the flyers and the sign-in sheet. I’ll send the final layout to the Events Centre on Monday morning unless either of you has a strong objection.

One thing to note – the confirmation mentions the room will be locked until 9:00 am, so the setup crew can’t get in any earlier. Tom, I know you’d mentioned coming in at 8:30 to set up the projector. Just flagging that we may need to shift that to 9:00. The AV gear is stored in the cabinet inside the room, so we can’t pre-stage it. I’ve left a note in the program calendar about the 9:00 access time so we don’t forget.

**2. Toddler Rhyme Time – Thursday 26 Nov, 11:00 am**

The usual room (Story Corner) is available, but the library’s cleaning schedule has been moved to Thursday mornings for the rest of November. That means the room won’t be vacuumed until after the session. I’ve asked the cleaners if they can do the room on Wednesday instead, but haven’t heard back yet. If they can’t change it, we might just need to do a quick once-over ourselves before the families arrive. I’ll update the calendar when I know more. The floor is usually fine, but there were some markers spilt last week and I’d rather not have little hands crawling around until it’s been properly cleaned.

**3. Monthly activity report – due Wednesday 25 Nov**

Just a reminder that the monthly activity report for October is due to the Council office by Wednesday, 25 November 2026. Priya, you’re the lead on this one, I think. The template is the same as last month – the one with the blue header and the sections for program attendance, room usage, and any incidents or feedback. I know you’d mentioned you were waiting on the final numbers from the school holiday sessions, so I’ve asked the front desk to send through their tallies by Monday. If they don’t come through, let me know and I can chase them.

An internal email notes Priya Singh report_due_date as 2026-11-25. Record status: current.

Also, I’ve attached the draft flyer for the Summer Reading Launch. I’ve used the new branding colours, but I’m not sure the font size on the date is big enough – it might look a bit small when printed at A5. Priya, you’re better at judging these things than I am. **Subject: RE: Program coordination – summer wrap-up and community feedback**

**From:** Priya Singh
**To:** Maya Chen; Tom Okafor
**Cc:**
**Date:** Tuesday, 24 November 2026, 3:42 PM

Hi Maya, Tom,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the roster notes – I’ve added everything to the shared calendar and I’ll chase Marcus and Aisha again tomorrow morning. Before we lock in the December schedule, I wanted to share some community feedback that came through over the last week. A few of these came in via the suggestion box, a couple were sent directly to the front desk, and one came through the library’s Facebook page. I’ve grouped them roughly by program area so we can decide what’s worth acting on before the summer rush.

**Feedback on recent programs**

1. **Seniors’ morning tea (Tuesday 10 November)** – One attendee, Margaret, left a note saying she really enjoyed the session but found the room a bit cold. She suggested we check the air-conditioning before next time. I’ve put a maintenance request in, but it might be worth adding “check room temp” to the run sheet for December. Nothing urgent, just a comfort thing.

2. **Baby Bounce (Thursday sessions)** – A parent, Sarah, emailed the front desk to say the 10:00 session has been filling up quickly and she’s been turned away twice. She asked if we could add a second session or increase the capacity. I know we’ve had this conversation before – the room can hold about 20 families comfortably, and we’re usually at that limit by 9:45. I’m not sure we can add another session without extra staff, but I thought it was worth raising again given the school holidays are coming.

3. **Lego Club (Saturday sessions)** – Tom, you mentioned you had a parent ask about age ranges after the last session. Just to confirm, the flyer says ages 5–12, but we’ve been letting younger siblings join in if they’re supervised. One parent suggested we put a sign up clarifying that, so we don’t get any awkward conversations at the door. Happy to draft something if you think it’s useful.

4. **Author talk (Wednesday 18 November)** – This one came through the Facebook page. A regular attendee, David, said he enjoyed the talk but would love to see more local authors in the program. He specifically mentioned a couple of names – I’ve pasted his comment below so you can see who he meant. I haven’t contacted anyone yet, but if we’re planning the autumn program soon, it might be worth reaching out.

> “Great session tonight. Would love to see more local writers – has the library thought about inviting [name] or [name]? Both have new books out and I think they’d draw a crowd.”

5. **Summer Reading Launch (Monday 28 December)** – We’ve had a few families RSVP already, which is great. One parent asked if there would be face painting again this year – I think we did that in 2024 but not last summer. I’ve noted it as a “maybe” on the planning doc. If we can get a volunteer or a local business to sponsor it, I’m happy to coordinate.

**Suggestions for future programs**

Alongside the feedback, there were a few broader ideas that came through – some more feasible than others. I’ve listed them below so you can see what’s been suggested and we can decide what to take forward.

- **A “Library 101” session for new migrants** – This came from a community worker who attends the English conversation group. She said a few of her clients have mentioned they’re not sure how to use the library catalogue or borrow e-books. We could run a simple workshop in January or February. I think this is a great idea, but I’d want to check with the outreach team to see if they’ve done something similar before.
